chapter: Clarinet and lessons with Jim Humphrey
title: Lessons from Professor Jim Humphrey; writing music from a graphophone
summary: He had no teacher on violin but studied clarinet with Humphrey, and wrote his own music while playing records on a graphophone to take to him.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Oh, well. Yes. Can you tell us about the, your lessons you mentioned yesterday? You had some lessons with, uh, old professor Jim Humphrey.
Humphrey, yes. Did you take any other lessons before that? No, sir, I hadn't. Only with Jim Humphrey.
When you started on the violin, did you have lessons right away on that, or? No, I didn't have no lesson. I didn't play.

Picked it up? Yeah, I just picked it up myself, but, uh, but Jim Humphrey was teaching, teaching me clarinet, you know? Well, he's the one who taught you clarinet then? After he died, I gave up all things, you know? Yeah. Yeah. But I used to write my own music and bring to him, you know? And he, you know, divided, you know?
Yes. You mentioned that you heard some, uh, music on the, uh, phonograph, the graphophone? Oh, yeah. I used to have a graphophone, you know?
I'd put it there, you know? Play a while and stop and write a while, you know? Yeah. And, and play it a while again and stop, you know?
Do you remember what pieces those were and what the band was that you heard playing?
No. I can't remember them pieces. It's been so long. Oh, yeah. It's been a long time. Yeah, and I never did bother with it after the old man passed out, you know?
Yeah. That's the, that music you would take up to Professor Humphrey, you told me yesterday.
